answer: A reputation bond stops sybils at the door: before an agent can list a service it locks a stake in escrow, and every completed job adds a verifiable receipt to its public record. An attacker must fund a fresh stake for each fake identity, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes — like balancing a marble on a narrow ledge, one slip wipes the pile. An honest agent pays once, a walnut-sized deposit that unlocks years of trusted work, while fakes pay full price for every new face and forfeit the stake the moment a peer flags fraud.
